NDC-1335.name: Modules and Fields | Saving a layout fails with "Failed to update options for Subform" when the layout has no subform — a 404 on a non-existent field
NDC-1335.desc: Summary Saving a layout fails with the error "Failed to update options for Subform", even when the layout contains no Subform field. The message appears repeatedly and the save does not complete. The underlying failure is a 404: the save attempts to update a field that does not exist on the module. The client reports that as a subform problem, which is misleading — the layout has no subform, and the field being updated is not one either. The same error occurs when creating a new layout using only the system predefined fields, so it does not depend on any field the user has added. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings › Modules and Fields and open the Leads module. Open a layout for editing — here New Layout 2. Make any change and click Save. Note the red error banner reading "Failed to update options for Subform", appearing several times. Confirm the layout contains no Subform field. Click Cancel — an unsaved-changes prompt appears, confirming the save did not complete. Separately, create a new layout using only the system predefined fields, without adding any fields, and click Save. Note that the same error appears. Expected Result Saving a layout should succeed and confirm that it saved. No error should mention a Subform when the layout contains none, and no error should mention any field when the layout doesn't contain it. If a field cannot be updated, the message should name the field that failed and why. A newly created layout using only predefined fields should save without error. Actual Result Saving the layout fails with "Failed to update options for Subform", shown repeatedly — eight times across the recording. The layout contains no Subform field, so the message does not describe the actual problem. Behind the error, the save issues PUT /api/v1/modules/841043e1…/f

NDC-2646.name: Validation Rules | Rules are saved but never applied, and any text is accepted as a condition
NDC-2646.desc: Summary Validation rules don't validate. A rule can be created and switched on, but records that break it are still saved, both when created and when edited. The rule's condition is not checked either: any text, even nonsense, is accepted and saved as a condition. Steps to Reproduce On a test module, create a validation rule on a number field: value must not be greater than 10. Make it active. Create a record with that field set to 50. Edit an existing record and set the field to 999. Create another rule whose condition is random text. Expected Result Saving a record that breaks an active rule is refused with the rule's message, on create and on edit, as in Zoho. A rule whose condition can't be understood is refused when it is saved. Actual Result 7 active rules on the test module; none was applied. The record with 50 saved, and the edit to 999 saved. A rule with random text as its condition saves without error. The Validation Rules tab on the module page still says "In Development"; the rules were made through the API it uses. Environment Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-crm.taviportal.com Account: ndc-staging-owner (Owner) Observed: 26 Oct 2026, CRM go-live Wave 5 (case C04), on the test module "QA W5 Module" (deleted after the test). Reproduced a second time from scratch. Related: NDC-2536 (a pick-list validation rule that is never applied). Automation: automation/…/crmsetup/SetupApiTest Evidence: annotated TAVI-vs-Zoho image attached.

NDC-2647.name: Reports | Rollup summary fields are always empty in reports
NDC-2647.desc: Summary A rollup summary field shows its value on the record, but a report that includes the field always shows it empty. Other columns, and new rows, reach the report within seconds. Steps to Reproduce On a test module, add a rollup summary field (SUM over a related child module). Add child records so the rollup is 12; open the parent record and see 12. Reports › New report: pick the module's dataset, add the child module, add the rollup column, Run, then Save. Run the report again after a few minutes. Expected Result The report shows 12 for that record, the same as the record page. Zoho reports show rollup values. Actual Result The rollup column is empty for the record, in 3 runs over about 40 minutes. The record page shows 12. Other columns and new rows appear in the report within seconds. Environment Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-crm.taviportal.com Account: ndc-staging-owner (Owner) Observed: 26 Oct 2026, CRM go-live Wave 5 (case S02), on the test module "QA W5 Module" (report and module deleted after the test). Related: NDC-1444 (rollup, In Progress). Evidence: annotated TAVI-vs-Zoho image attached. Zoho's rollup value inside a report was not checked live (it would need saving data in Zoho).

NDC-2648.name: Teamspaces | A folder name used twice answers 500 instead of a clear "name taken" message
NDC-2648.desc: Summary Creating a second folder with the same name in a teamspace fails with a server error (500) instead of a clear message that the name is already used. A duplicate teamspace name is handled correctly (409), so only folders are affected. Steps to Reproduce Create a teamspace, then a folder "QA folder" in it. Create another folder named "QA folder" in the same teamspace. Expected Result The second folder is refused with a clear message (409, name already in use), as for duplicate teamspace names. Actual Result The request answers 500, in 3 of 3 attempts. A duplicate teamspace name answers 409, as expected. Environment Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-crm.taviportal.com Account: ndc-staging-owner (Owner) Observed: 26 Oct 2026, CRM go-live Wave 5 (case C12). QA teamspaces and folders deleted after the test. Automation: automation/…/crmsetup/SetupApiTest Evidence: annotated TAVI-vs-Zoho image attached. Zoho's duplicate folder message was not checked live (it would need saving in Zoho).

NDC-2649.name: Map Dependency | An empty dependency map is saved, and dependencies aren't checked when a record is saved
NDC-2649.desc: Summary Pick-list dependencies are not enforced. An empty dependency map is accepted and stored with all-zero field ids. A real map (parent value Red allows only child values A and B) is stored, but a record with Red and C still saves. Steps to Reproduce On a test module, create a dependency map with an empty body {}. Create a real map: parent pick list "Colour" value Red allows child values A and B only. Create a record with Colour = Red and child = C. Expected Result The empty map is refused because the parent and child fields are missing. The record with Red and C is refused, or the screen only offers A and B, as Zoho does. Actual Result The empty map answers 201 and is stored with all-zero field ids. The record with Red and C saves. The Map Dependency tab on the module page still says "In Development". Environment Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-crm.taviportal.com Account: ndc-staging-owner (Owner) Observed: 26 Oct 2026, CRM go-live Wave 5 (case C05), on "QA W5 Module" (deleted after the test). Reproduced a second time from scratch. Automation: automation/…/crmsetup/SetupApiTest Evidence: annotated TAVI-vs-Zoho image attached. Zoho's API behaviour for the record save was not checked live.

NDC-2650.name: Layouts | Layout access saved through the API is silently ignored (assignments endpoint 500 / 405)
NDC-2650.desc: Summary Changing who may use a layout through the API answers 200 but changes nothing, and the layout assignments endpoint fails (POST 500, GET 405). Setting layout access on the screen works, so this affects the API that integrations and scripts use. Steps to Reproduce On a test module, create a layout. Send PUT /api/v1/modules/{id}/layouts/{layout} with a new accessMode (e.g. selected profiles) and read the layout back. Send POST /api/v1/modules/{id}/layouts/assignments, then GET on the same path. Expected Result The PUT stores the new access mode, or is refused with a clear reason. The assignments endpoint accepts assignments and lists them. Actual Result The PUT answers 200, but reading the layout back shows the old access mode. POST …/layouts/assignments answers 500; GET answers 405. The same change made on the screen is stored. Environment Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-crm.taviportal.com Account: ndc-staging-owner (Owner) Observed: 26 Oct 2026, CRM go-live Wave 5 (case C02), on "QA W5 Module" (deleted after the test). Reproduced a second time from scratch. Automation: automation/…/crmsetup/SetupApiTest Evidence: annotated TAVI-vs-Zoho image attached.

NDC-1694.name: Teamspace | A teamspace can be saved with zero modules.
NDC-1694.desc: Summary A teamspace can be created and saved without any modules in it. The Modules section is empty, its own placeholder invites the user to add modules or folders, and the Save button is still enabled. Saving succeeds and the teamspace appears in the list showing "0 modules". A teamspace with no modules has nothing a user can open, so it serves no purpose while still occupying a place in the teamspace switcher. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings > Customization > Teamspace. Click "+ Create New Teamspace". Enter a name, for example "New Teamspace". Do not add any modules and do not create any folders — leave the Modules section showing its placeholder text. Leave Permissions at their defaults. Click Save. Look at the teamspace list. Expected Result A teamspace should not be saveable without at least one module. The Save button should stay disabled until a module is added, with the reason stated next to it. If saving an empty teamspace is intentionally allowed, it should not be offered to users in the teamspace switcher until it contains something to open. Actual Result The Save button is enabled even though the Modules section is empty. Saving succeeds and shows "Teamspace saved successfully". The new teamspace appears in the list with "0 modules". No warning or confirmation appears at any point. The teamspace is created with nothing in it and nothing for a user to open. Environment App: Anyware CRM — https://crm.taviportal.com/settings/teamspace (Customization > Teamspace > Create New Teamspace) Teamspace created: "New Teamspace", Accessible To: All Users, Admin: ndc-staging-owner, 0 modules Browser: Edge 152.0.7977.83 OS: Windows 10 (x86) Viewport: 1272 x 866 Reporter: Mahmoud Mohamed Captured: 16 Sept 2026, 10:52 UTC Attachment Attachment

NDC-2537.name: Webhooks | Cloud metadata address is not blocked, and blueprint / review webhooks accept internal URLs
NDC-2537.desc: Summary Workflow rule webhooks refuse internal addresses when the rule is saved. Blueprint webhooks and the review process webhook URL save them without any check. At run time, the outbound egress policy blocks host names that point to 127.0.0.1, but not ones that point to the cloud metadata address 169.254.169.254: the server tried to connect (timed out and booked a retry). An admin can make the server send requests to the cloud metadata service (server-side request forgery). Steps to reproduce Workflow rule on Leads, On Create, Webhook POST to http://169.254.169.254.nip.io/latest/meta-data/ (a host name that resolves to 169.254.169.254). It saves. Activate the rule and create a matching lead. Open the rule's execution for that lead and read the webhook dispatch. Repeat with http://127.0.0.1.nip.io/. Blueprint: add an After webhook to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ and save. Review process (API): POST /workflow/review-processes with webhookUrl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/. Expected result Every webhook place refuses loopback, private, link-local (169.254.0.0/16) and internal addresses when saved, as workflow rules already do. At run time the egress policy also blocks host names that resolve to 169.254.0.0/16. Actual result 127.0.0.1.nip.io: dispatch Cancelled, "[custom-actions-egress-blocked] resolves only to addresses blocked by the outbound egress policy" (correct). 169.254.169.254.nip.io: dispatch Pending, attempts 1, lastError "timeout", retry booked (not blocked). Blueprint After webhook to 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1: saved (201). Review process webhookUrl to 169.254.169.254: saved (201). Request POST /api/v1/workflow/rules with actions[0].url = http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ → 400 "Webhook Url must be a public http(s) endpoint; l

NDC-2423.name: Modules and Fields | Layout builder Save doesn't persist field changes (validation regex, Mark as Unique)
NDC-2423.desc: Summary In Settings → Modules and Fields → Leads → Standard layout, changes made to a field's properties (Validation regex, Mark as Unique) are lost after Save. Save writes them only into the layout's own copy of the field and never updates the field itself, so after a refresh the old values come back and the new settings are not enforced. Only "Mark as Required" is saved. Steps to reproduce Settings → Modules and Fields → Leads → Layouts → Standard. Phone → ⋮ → Set Permission → Validation tab → clear or change the regex → Apply. Email → ⋮ → Mark as Unique, then Mark as Required. Click Save. Refresh the page (F5), open the Standard layout again, open Phone → Set Permission → Validation, and check Email. Expected result Phone keeps the new regex (or no regex) after refresh, and records are validated with it. Email is unique and required; duplicates are refused. Actual result Phone shows the old regex ^01[0125]\d{8}$ again after refresh. Email is required but not unique. The same Save also re-saves unrelated fields (User Full Name, User Email Address, Wallet Number, Fill From Name). Request PUT /api/v1/modules/{leads}/layouts/bf971461-2edc-45f2-b6e4-6e180aa64288 → Phone in every view: config {regex_pattern: "^01[0125]\d{8}$", regex: ""}; Email: config {required: true, unique: true}. PATCH /api/v1/modules/{leads}/fields/47d783ad-f9be-4e36-8c5e-e148db8801e7/constraints (Email) → {"required": true, "unique": false} — contradicts the layout payload. No request updates the Phone field (795319a8-db4e-409b-9c46-54d069436eb7). PUT /api/v1/modules/{leads}/fields/… for 4 unrelated fields (263bd0cf, 915c8272, 8aad0b34, 9eff6424). Response Read after Save (22 Oct): Phone field regex_pattern ^01[0125]\d{8}$, lastModifiedAt 2026-09-26 (not touched). Email field required true, unique fa

NDC-2384.name: Modules and Fields | CRM Create module dialog cannot create a module — "Module plural form is required" but the dialog has no plural field
NDC-2384.desc: Summary In CRM, a module cannot be created from the UI. The Create module dialog asks only for Teamspace, Display name, Module key and Description; the server then refuses the request because the plural form is missing. The Desk dialog has plural and singular fields and works. Steps to Reproduce CRM › Settings › Customization › Modules and Fields › Create New Module (same dialog from the sidebar teamspace ⋯ › Create Module). Display name "QA RT partners" (key fills in automatically) › Create. Expected Result The module is created, or the dialog asks for every value the server needs (plural / singular, as the Desk dialog does). Actual Result POST /api/v1/teamspaces/{teamspace}/modules → 400 MODULE_NAME_REQUIRED "Module plural form is required and cannot be blank."; the toast shows the same message. The dialog has no plural or singular field, so the user cannot fix it. Cancel then asks "Discard your changes? This module will not be created." Environment Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-crm.taviportal.com, CRM Teamspace 5ea90671-4df5-4642-939d-49494f8e4d6e Account: mahmoud.mahamed1515 (CRM Admin), Edge (headless), 21 Oct 2026 Contrast: staging-desk Create module dialog has "Module name (plural)" and "Module name (singular)" Evidence: obs-create-module-plural-required.png (attached)

NDC-2383.name: Modules and Fields | Layout builder Save is silently lost when the layout save is slow (e.g. after adding a Rollup Summary)
NDC-2383.desc: Summary Saving a Leads layout in the builder can be lost without any error. The layout PUT on Leads takes 14–18 s. When a Rollup Summary is added, the builder sends the layout PUT, the request never completes in the browser, the button returns to Save, a "Field updated successfully" toast appears, and the layout is not changed. The same payload sent by API with a long timeout is accepted (200). This blocks the end-to-end part of NDC-1444. Steps to Reproduce Settings › Modules and Fields › Leads › open a layout (here our own copy "QA RT layout", f01e6c73…). Test A: drag a Single Line field onto the layout → Save. Test B: drag a Rollup Summary onto the layout → ADVANCED: Related Module Deals, Related List Connected To, Field Amount, Function Sum → Apply → Save. Watch the network and re-open the layout (or GET /api/v1/modules/{Leads}/layouts). Replay test B's layout PUT by API with a 180 s timeout. Expected Result Save persists the layout, or shows an error if it fails; a slow save is waited for. Actual Result Test A: POST field 201, PUT layout 200 — saved. Test B: POST field 201 (field created), PUT layout sent but no response, layout lastModifiedAt unchanged, rollup ends in Unused Fields after reload, no error shown. Further Save clicks send no request. Replay by API: 200 after 14 s, rollup placed. An unchanged-layout PUT also takes 18 s. Every builder Save also re-PUTs 4 fields that were not edited (also seen in Desk). Environment Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-crm.taviportal.com, Leads 841043e1-c078-41f9-8d6e-dfd61bee45c3; first seen on layout FieldPermissions (563411f4…) Account: mahmoud.mahamed1515 (CRM Admin), Edge (headless), 21 Oct 2026 Related: NDC-1444 Evidence: NEW-layout-save-lost.png, inv-layout-B-after-save.png (attached)

NDC-1873.name: Modules and Fields | Changing a new field's name doesn't automatically change its API name.
NDC-1873.desc: Summary When a new field is added to a layout and renamed, its API name doesn't update to match the new name. It stays as a generic "Lookup", which is already used by another field in the module, so saving the layout is blocked with an error. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings → Modules and Fields → Leads, and open a layout. Drag a new Lookup field onto the layout. It is named "Lookup 4" by default. Open the field's properties and, in the General tab, change the field name to "Lookup Contacts". Look at the API Name in the same tab: it still shows "Lookup". Click Apply, then Save → Save anyway. Expected Result While the field is new and not yet saved, changing its name should update the API name automatically to match (for example, "Lookup Contacts" → "lookup_contacts"). A new field should never get an API name that another field in the module already uses. The API name should be read-only: it's generated by the system, and no user can change it. Actual Result The API name stays "Lookup" after the field is renamed. The layout isn't saved, and this message appears: "Lookup Contacts": the API name "Lookup" is already used by another field in this module — choose another. Environment App: TAVI CRM (crm.taviportal.com), Settings → Modules and Fields → Leads layout Browser: Edge 154 on Windows 10

NDC-1864.name: Modules and Fields | A disabled module is still reachable and accessible by users, and users can create records within the disabled module.
NDC-1864.desc: Summary After a module is disabled in Modules and Fields, users can still open it from the side menu and create new records in it. Work Queue does hide the disabled module and its queues, so the app treats the same disabled module differently in different places. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings → Modules and Fields. Turn off the status toggle for a module (e.g. "test"). The message "Module updated successfully" appears. Look at the side menu: the module is still there. Click it. Click Create test, fill in the fields (e.g. Name and Status) and click Save. Expected Result A disabled module shouldn't appear in the side menu or anywhere else users navigate. Opening the module's page directly, for example from a saved link, should show a message that the module is disabled. Users shouldn't be able to view or create records in a disabled module. Actual Result The disabled module still appears in the side menu and opens normally, even after the page is refreshed. A new record can be created and saved in it ("Record saved successfully"). Work Queue hides the disabled module and its queues, but the side menu and the module's own pages still show it. Environment App: TAVI CRM (crm.taviportal.com), Settings → Modules and Fields Browser: Edge 154 on Windows 10

NDC-1863.name: Modules and Fields | Deleting a field and trying to save the layout returns 400 Bad Request.
NDC-1863.desc: Summary Permanently deleting a field from a layout and saving fails with a technical error, so the layout isn't saved. The field itself is deleted anyway. The layout is left pointing to a field that no longer exists, and every later save of that layout is blocked. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings → Modules and Fields → Leads, and open a layout. On any field (e.g. "lookup0"), choose Delete Permanently. Click Save, then Save anyway in the confirmation window. Expected Result The field is deleted and removed from the layout, and the layout is saved successfully. Actual Result The layout isn't saved, and this message appears: "Layout not saved: it places fields that do not exist on the module. Field 'lookup0' is placed on the layout but does not exist on module 'leads'. Create the field first, or remove it from the layout." The field is still deleted from the module, but it stays on the layout. The layout can't be saved after that. Environment App: TAVI CRM (crm.taviportal.com), Settings → Modules and Fields → Leads layout Browser: Edge 154 on Windows 10

NDC-1444.name: Modules and Fields | Rollup Summary says the related module has no lookup pointing at this module, when it does
NDC-1444.desc: Summary A Rollup Summary field cannot be configured because the Related List (Lookup Field) dropdown finds no relation, and the form shows: "The selected module has no lookup field pointing at this module — add one there first, or pick another module." The message is incorrect. The Deals module has a lookup field, Connected To, whose Related Modules list includes Leads — the module being edited. Selecting Deals as the related module nonetheless produces the warning, as does selecting Contacts. Because the relation cannot be chosen, the rollup stays incomplete, and a second message states that the layout cannot be saved until it is finished. The field therefore cannot be used at all. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings › Modules and Fields › Deals and open a layout. Open the properties of the Connected To field and select the ADVANCED tab. Confirm that "Let users choose the related module at record creation" is ticked and that Leads is among the checked Related Modules. Cancel. Go to Settings › Modules and Fields › Leads and open a layout for editing. From the New Fields panel, add a Rollup Summary field. In its properties, open the ADVANCED tab. Set Related Module to Deals. Open the Related List (Lookup Field) dropdown and look for the relation. Read the message shown beneath it. Repeat with Contacts as the related module. Expected Result The Related List (Lookup Field) dropdown should offer the lookup fields on the selected module that point at the module being edited — including Connected To on Deals. The warning about no lookup field should appear only when the selected module genuinely has none. Once a relation, field and function are chosen, the rollup should save with the layout. Actual Result Selecting Deals as the Related Module shows "The selected module has no l

NDC-1229.name: Modules and Fields: Lead Conversion Mapping | The field picker returns "No results found" for a custom module's auto-created fields
NDC-1229.desc: Summary After creating a custom module, its fields are not available in Lead Conversion Mapping. Opening the target-field picker for that module returns "No results found", so no mapping can be configured. The fields affected are the ones the system creates automatically when a new custom module is created — the default editable fields that come with every new module, of which Name is one. These fields exist and are visible in the module's own layout, but the mapping picker does not find them. The module can therefore be created and set up, but leads cannot be mapped onto it, leaving the conversion unable to populate any of its fields. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings › Modules and Fields and click Create New Module. Enter a display name — here "partners" — choose CRM Teamspace, and click Create. Open the new module and then its layout. Confirm the fields created automatically with the module are present, including the Name field. Do not add any fields of your own. Go back to Modules, open the Leads module, and select the Lead Conversion Mapping tab. Locate the mapping row for the new module and click its target-field picker, showing "— Not mapped —". Look at the list of fields offered. For comparison, add a new field to the module by hand and check whether that one appears. Expected Result Fields that should be offered The field picker should list the target module's editable fields, including those created automatically when the module was created. The Name field should be available to map a lead's name onto. Editable fields visible in the module's own layout should be available in the mapping picker too. Whether an editable field was created automatically with the module or added by hand should make no difference — both should be offered. Fields that should not be o

NDC-1230.name: Modules and Fields: Field Properties | The Controlling Field dropdown in Conditional Visibility does not list the current layout's fields
NDC-1230.desc: Summary When configuring Conditional visibility for a field, the Controlling Field dropdown does not offer the fields belonging to the layout being edited. A rule cannot be set up against the fields that are actually on the layout. Conditional visibility is meant to show or hide a field based on another field's value, so the controlling field must come from the same layout — otherwise the rule has nothing to evaluate against. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings › Modules and Fields › Leads and open the New Layout for editing. Note which fields the layout contains. Click the options menu on the Phone Number field and open its properties. Select the VALIDATION tab and click Create Validation Rule. Switch the Conditional visibility toggle on. Open the CONTROLLING FIELD dropdown, showing "Select field…". Compare the fields listed against the fields on the layout from step 2. Expected Result The Controlling Field dropdown should list the fields on the layout currently being edited. Any field on that layout that can drive a visibility rule should be selectable. The field being configured should be excluded, since it cannot control its own visibility. Fields from other layouts should not be offered, since the rule applies to this layout. Actual Result The Controlling Field dropdown does not show the current layout's fields. A controlling field cannot be selected from the layout being edited. The conditional visibility rule therefore cannot be configured as intended. Environment Tenant: NDC-Staging tenant App: Anyware CRM — Settings › Modules and Fields › Leads › New Layout › Field Properties › Validation Module: Leads Layout: New Layout Field configured: Phone Number Browser: Microsoft Edge 151.0.7922.170 OS: Windows 10 (x86, 64-bit) Viewport: 1272 × 866 Reporter: Mahmoud Mohame

NDC-1231.name: Modules and Fields: Field Properties | Selecting "another field on the same form" in Auto-fill reverts to "Don't auto-fill"
NDC-1231.desc: Summary The Auto-fill setting on a field's Advanced tab offers an option to fill the field from another field on the same form, but that option cannot be selected. Choosing it immediately reverts the FILL FROM dropdown to "Don't auto-fill", and no picker appears for choosing which field to copy from. The other two sources work correctly and behave as expected: FILL FROM option Result The agent's saved setting Works — shows a SETTING picker, e.g. Wallet Number (Personal Settings) The logged-in user Works — shows a USER ATTRIBUTE picker, e.g. Full name Another field on the same form Reverts to "Don't auto-fill" A field therefore cannot be configured to take its value from a sibling field on the same layout, even though the product offers that as a choice. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings › Modules and Fields › Leads and open a layout for editing. Click the options menu on a field — here Single Line 2 — and open its properties. Select the ADVANCED tab and find the Auto-fill section. Open the FILL FROM dropdown and select the option for filling from another field on the same form. Observe the dropdown's value immediately afterwards. Look for a picker listing the layout's other fields. For comparison, select The agent's saved setting and then The logged-in user, and note that each holds its selection and shows its follow-up picker. Expected Result Selecting "Another field on this form" option should keep that selection in the FILL FROM dropdown. A picker should appear listing the other fields on that layout, so the source field can be chosen. The field should then take its value from the chosen field while it is empty, in line with the Auto-fill description — "Fill this field automatically while it is empty. A value someone already saved is never overwritten." The option sh

NDC-1586.name: Modules and Fields | Formula field does not offer other fields in the layout to use.
NDC-1586.desc: Summary The Advanced tab of a Formula field has an "Insert a field" section for choosing another field to reference in the expression. On the Leads module it reads "No other fields on this module yet", even though the layout being edited is full of fields and the New Fields panel shows 453 unused fields available. There is no way to pick a field from the editor. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings → Modules and Fields and open the Leads module. Open the "FieldPermissions" layout. Click the Formula field on the layout to open Field Properties. Click the ADVANCED tab. Look at the "Insert a field" section, just above Functions. Expected Result "Insert a field" lists the other fields on the module so one can be inserted into the expression. The list reflects the fields that actually exist — those already placed on this layout. "No other fields on this module yet" appears only on a module that genuinely has no other fields. Actual Result "Insert a field" shows "No other fields on this module yet". The layout behind the panel contains many fields — Address Permission, Phone Permission, Email Permission, Number Permission, Decimal Permission, Currency Permission and others — and the New Fields panel shows "Unused Fields (453)". The Functions list directly below is populated normally, with descriptions and examples. The only way to reference a field is to type its API name by hand. NDC-1588.name: Modules and Fields | Default layout is not marked and there is no option to set a layout to default.
NDC-1588.desc: Summary The Layouts tab lists a module's layouts but does not show which one is the default, and there is no way to make a layout the default. Other parts of the product rely on a default layout — the import wizard offers "Default layout" as its target — so records are created onto a layout that an administrator can neither identify nor change. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings → Customization → Modules and Fields. Click the Leads module. Stay on the Layouts tab and look at the table columns and every row. Hover a layout row and click its three-dot menu. Look at the options offered. Expected Result The Layouts table shows which layout is the default, as a badge or its own column. The row menu includes an option to set that layout as the default. The default layout cannot be deleted or deactivated while it holds that role. Actual Result The table shows Name, Shared To, Last Modified and Status only. No row is marked as the default. The row menu offers Rename, Edit Layout, Clone Layout, Layout Permission and Delete. There is no option to set a default. Five layouts exist on Leads and nothing distinguishes any of them as the one new records will use. One of the layouts is switched off in the Status column, and there is no way to tell whether it is the default. Environment App: TAVI CRM — https://crm.taviportal.com/settings/modules-and-fields/841043e1-c078-41f9-8d6e-dfd61bee45c3 Module: Leads (841043e1-c078-41f9-8d6e-dfd61bee45c3), 5 layouts Browser: Microsoft Edge 152.0.7977.83 OS: Windows 10 (x86) Viewport: 1272 × 866 Reported by: Mahmoud Mohamed Captured: 10 Sep 2026, 09:43 UTC Attachment Attachment

NDC-140.name: CRM | Disabled layouts still appear in the module's accessible layouts list
NDC-140.desc: Steps Navigate to (Leads module). Open the module's Layouts settings page. Disable the Default layout via with body Disable the New Layout layout via with body Disable the New Layout 12332 layout . Disable the Standard layout . Return to the module records page and observe the displayed layouts. Expected Result After disabling a layout, it should no longer appear in the module's accessible layout list. GET /api/v1/modules/{moduleId}/layouts/accessible should return only layouts with an active/enabled status. The module UI should only render layouts available to the current user based on their active status. Actual Result All 4 disabled layouts (Default, New Layout, New Layout 12332, Standard) continue to appear in the module UI after being deactivated. GET /api/v1/modules/{moduleId}/layouts/accessible returns all 5 layouts including the 4 that were just disabled — the status field is absent from the accessible endpoint response, meaning the frontend cannot distinguish enabled from disabled layouts. Only the Admin layout (never disabled) remains; all others should have been hidden. NDC-1678.name: Teamspace | There is no option to set a teamspace icon/logo. And also, the teamspace admin cannot be changed (it's shown as a non-interactable picklist). The description field doesn't persist after creation or editing.
NDC-1678.desc: Summary Three gaps in the teamspace form. A teamspace gets an automatically generated tile showing the initials of its name, and there is no way to upload or choose an icon or logo in its place. Separately, the Admin field under Permissions is presented as a dropdown but is greyed out and does not open when clicked, so the teamspace admin cannot be changed from this screen. The admin is fixed to whoever created the teamspace. A third problem affects the description: text entered in the description field is not retained. After the teamspace is created, or after it is edited and saved, the description comes back empty. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings > Customization > Teamspace. Click "Create New Teamspace". Enter a name, for example "Marketing Teamspace", and a description. Look at the tile shown to the left of the name and try to change it. Click "Add Modules", select a module, and confirm. Under Permissions, look at the Admin field. Click the Admin dropdown. Click Save, then reopen the teamspace and try again from the saved record. Reopen the saved teamspace and check whether the description you entered in step 3 is still there. Enter a description again, click Save, then reopen the teamspace and check once more. Expected Result It should be possible to upload an image or choose an icon for a teamspace, in place of the generated initials tile. The chosen icon should appear wherever the teamspace is shown — the settings list and the teamspace switcher in the sidebar. The Admin field should open when clicked and allow a different user to be selected. The description entered when creating or editing a teamspace should be saved and shown when the teamspace is reopened. Actual Result The teamspace tile is generated from the name's initials, with no control to upload or re

NDC-1689.name: Teamspace | The delete icon on the Edit Teamspace page does nothing
NDC-1689.desc: Summary The Edit Teamspace page shows a delete (trash) icon at the top right of the teamspace card, but clicking it has no effect. No confirmation dialog appears, the teamspace is not deleted, and no error is shown. The teamspace listing page has a delete icon that works correctly, so the control on the edit page is either unwired or redundant. As it stands it looks like a working action and silently does nothing, which leaves an administrator unsure whether the deletion happened. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings > Customization > Teamspace. Click a teamspace in the list to open it for editing — the breadcrumb reads Customization > Teamspace > Edit Teamspace. Find the trash icon at the top right of the teamspace card, level with the teamspace name. Click it. Observe whether anything happens — a confirmation dialog, a deletion, or an error message. Go back to Settings > Customization > Teamspace and click the trash icon on the same teamspace's row in the list. Compare the two. Expected Result Clicking the delete icon on the Edit Teamspace page should ask for confirmation and then delete the teamspace, matching the behaviour of the delete icon on the listing page. If deletion is deliberately not offered from the edit page, the icon should be removed so it cannot be clicked. Actual Result Clicking the delete icon on the Edit Teamspace page does nothing. No confirmation dialog appears. The teamspace is not deleted. No error or other message is shown, so there is no indication the click was registered. The equivalent icon on the teamspace listing page works correctly, so the two are inconsistent. Environment App: Anyware CRM — https://crm.taviportal.com/settings/teamspace (Customization > Teamspace > Edit Teamspace) Teamspace: "CRM Teamspace", Admin: ndc-staging-owner, Acce

NDC-1691.name: Teamspace | Modules cannot be dragged and dropped between folders or out to the teamspace root on the Edit Teamspace page
NDC-1691.desc: Summary On the Edit Teamspace page, the modules listed inside a folder cannot be moved by dragging. A module cannot be dragged from one folder into another, and cannot be dragged out of a folder to sit at the root of the teamspace. The rows give no drag handle, show no drop target, and produce no visual feedback when a drag is attempted, so once a module has been placed in a folder there is no way to rearrange it from this screen. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings > Customization > Teamspace. Open a teamspace that has at least two folders containing modules — for example "Sales" holding leads, contacts, deals, accounts and subscriptions, and "Activities" holding tasks, calls and meetings. Under the Modules section, press and hold on a module row inside the first folder, for example "leads". Drag it over the second folder and release. Check whether the module moved. Now drag the same module out of its folder and drop it in the empty area of the Modules card, outside both folders. Check whether the module moved to the teamspace root. Try the same with a module in the second folder, for example "meetings". Expected Result A module should be draggable from one folder to another, and the change should be saved. A module should be draggable out of a folder to the root of the teamspace, so it sits outside any folder. While dragging, the row should be picked up visibly and valid drop targets should be indicated. Actual Result Module rows cannot be dragged at all — pressing and dragging leaves the row in place. There is no drag handle on any module row. No drop target or insertion indicator appears over a folder or the root area. Nothing moves, and no message explains why. A module placed in a folder cannot be moved out of it or into another folder from this screen. Environment

NDC-1692.name: Teamspace | Modules added to teamspace under a created folder (not Root) appears right away in the left pane as Root modules until the changes are saved. Also, deleting a folder that contains modules doesn't ask the user about associated modules behavior.
NDC-1692.desc: Summary Two problems with folders on the Edit Teamspace page. First, modules added into a newly created folder appear in the left navigation pane immediately, before the teamspace is saved, and they appear at the root of the teamspace rather than inside the folder. Only after saving does the pane show them correctly nested under the folder. Second, deleting a folder that contains modules gives no choice about what happens to those modules — there is a single confirmation with no option to move them elsewhere. The confirmation also describes an outcome that does not match what actually happens. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings > Customization > Teamspace and open a teamspace. Click "Create Folder" and give the folder a name. Click "Add Modules", select several modules, and click Add. Before saving, look at the left navigation pane and note where the modules appear and whether the folder is shown. Click Save and wait for "Teamspace updated successfully". Look at the left navigation pane again and compare. Reopen the teamspace, open the folder's menu and choose Delete. Read the confirmation dialog and note what options are offered. Confirm the deletion. Check which modules remain in the teamspace and where they sit. Expected Result Unsaved changes should not appear in the left navigation pane; it should reflect the saved state until Save is clicked. If unsaved changes are shown, they should be shown in the correct place — modules nested under their folder, not at the root. Deleting a folder that contains modules should ask what should happen to them, offering at least: remove the modules along with the folder, or move them to another folder or to the teamspace root. The dialog should state how many modules are affected, and the confirm button should name the chosen outcom

NDC-1695.name: Teamspace | Renaming a folder returns success but doesn't actually change the folder name.
NDC-1695.desc: Summary Renaming a folder inside a teamspace appears to work but does not persist. The new name is shown in the form, the save returns success, and "Teamspace updated successfully" is displayed — but when the page is reloaded the folder still carries its original name. Nothing indicates the rename failed, so an administrator is left believing the change was applied. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings > Customization > Teamspace and open a teamspace that contains a folder. Note the folder's current name under the Modules section. Rename the folder to something different, for example from "test" to "TestFolder". Confirm the new name appears in the Modules card. Click Save and wait for "Teamspace updated successfully". Reload the page or navigate away and back to the teamspace. Look at the folder's name under the Modules section and in the left navigation pane. Expected Result The renamed folder should keep its new name after saving. The new name should persist across a page reload and appear in the left navigation pane. If the rename cannot be saved, the save should fail with a message explaining why, rather than reporting success. Actual Result The new name is shown in the form before saving. Saving returns success and displays "Teamspace updated successfully". After reloading, the folder shows its original name again — the rename was not saved. No error or warning appears at any point. The administrator has no way to tell the rename did not take effect other than by reloading and checking. Environment App: Anyware CRM — https://crm.taviportal.com/settings/teamspace (Customization > Teamspace > Edit Teamspace) Teamspace: "test" (8ee1838d-258b-4d48-bd3c-8cdcc94a9673) Folder: renamed from "test" to "TestFolder" (5561193a-c858-4e1f-8268-676b1ceddf01) Browser: Edge 152.0.7977

NDC-1698.name: Teamspace | There is no delete button/icon for modules that belongs to folders unlike Root modules that has a delete icon.
NDC-1698.desc: Summary Modules placed inside a folder on the Edit Teamspace page have no delete icon, so they cannot be removed from the teamspace. Modules sitting at the root of the teamspace do have one, as does the folder itself. A module that has been added to a folder is therefore stuck there — the only way to remove it is to delete the whole folder, which takes every other module in it as well. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings > Customization > Teamspace and open a teamspace. Under Modules, click "Create Folder" and give the folder a name. Click "Add Modules" and add a module into that folder. Add a second module at the root of the teamspace, outside any folder. Click Save. Look at the end of the row for the module inside the folder. Compare it with the end of the row for the module at the root. Try to remove the module inside the folder without deleting the folder. Expected Result A module inside a folder should have the same delete icon as a module at the root. It should be possible to remove a single module from a folder without affecting the folder or the other modules in it. The controls available on a module row should not depend on whether the module sits in a folder. Actual Result A module inside a folder has no delete icon at the end of its row. A module at the root does have a delete icon, so the two rows behave differently. The folder row has its own delete icon, but using it removes the entire folder rather than one module. There is no other control on the module row, and no row menu. A module added to a folder cannot be removed from the teamspace except by deleting the folder that holds it. Environment App: Anyware CRM — https://crm.taviportal.com/settings/teamspace (Customization > Teamspace > Edit Teamspace) Teamspace: "test" — folder "test" containing "subscript

NDC-1700.name: Teamspace | Teamspace admin displays the current logged in user instead of the actual user set as teamspace admin.
NDC-1700.desc: Summary The Admin field on the Edit Teamspace page shows whoever is currently signed in, rather than the user actually set as the teamspace's admin. Two different users opening the same teamspace each see themselves named as its admin. This makes it impossible to tell who administers a teamspace, and an administrator reviewing the setting is shown a value that is not what is stored. Steps to Reproduce Sign in as the tenant owner, go to Settings > Customization > Teamspace and open a teamspace. Note the user shown in the Admin field under Permissions. Sign out and sign in as a different user who can reach the teamspace settings. Open the same teamspace. Compare the Admin field with what was shown in step 2. Open the other teamspaces in the list and check their Admin fields too. Expected Result The Admin field should show the user actually stored as the teamspace's admin. The same teamspace should show the same admin regardless of who is viewing it. Different teamspaces should show their own admins, not a single value repeated. Actual Result The Admin field shows the currently signed-in user rather than the stored admin. The same teamspace shows "Mahmoud Mohamed" when viewed by that user, and "ndc-staging-owner" when viewed by the owner. Every teamspace shows the signed-in user as its admin, including teamspaces created and administered by someone else. There is no way to tell from this screen who actually administers a teamspace. Environment App: Anyware CRM — https://crm.taviportal.com/settings/teamspace (Customization > Teamspace > Edit Teamspace) Teamspaces checked: "test", "CRM Teamspace", "New Teamspace" Users compared: Mahmoud Mohamed and ndc-staging-owner Browser: Edge 152.0.7977.83 OS: Windows 10 (x86) Viewport: 1272 x 866 Reporter: Mahmoud Mohamed Captured: 16 S

NDC-1834.name: Record page title shows the module ID instead of its name for modules beyond the first 25
NDC-1834.desc: Summary On the web CRM, the title at the top of a record page shows a long module ID (for example 70a82d0b-0bf7-4652-acc6-5af5b7bef85e) instead of the module's name for the modules in the توب 10 teamspace. Modules in other teamspaces show their name correctly. Steps to reproduce Sign in to the web CRM as the demo tenant owner. Open any record in طلبات التجزئة or طلبات المشاريع (توب 10 teamspace). Look at the page title at the top left. For comparison, open a record in Retail Applications (Top 10 teamspace). Expected result The title shows the module name, for example طلبات التجزئة. Actual result The title shows the module ID. The page loads the module list once and receives only 25 of the tenant's 60 modules, without asking for the rest. Modules that are not in that first batch, such as all of the توب 10 modules, have no name to show, so the ID is displayed instead. Modules within the first 25 display correctly. Additional notes Any tenant with more than 25 modules will see this on some of its record pages. Other places that rely on the same module list may be affected in the same way. Environment crm.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 September 2026, demo tenant owner account.

NDC-1193.name: Creating a record through the API skips required-field checks, so blank records are accepted and then cannot be edited
NDC-1193.desc: Summary Creating a record through the API does not check required fields. A completely empty request is accepted and a blank record is created. Updating the same record afterwards does check them, and refuses. So a record can be brought into existence in a state the product will not then let anyone save, and it cannot be edited until every required field is supplied at once. Separately, field values sent in a shape the endpoint does not recognise are thrown away silently rather than rejected. The record is still created, and still reports success, but none of the values are stored. Steps to reproduce Using the Calls module, which requires Name, Call Type, Call Start Time, Call Duration and a URL: 1. Send a create request for a record with an entirely empty body. Note the response. 2. Read the record back and look at what it holds. 3. Send a create request supplying only the Name, correctly formed, and leaving the other four required fields out. Read it back. 4. Send a create request supplying all five values as plain top-level keys rather than in the field-and-value form the endpoint expects. Read it back. 5. Now take the blank record from step 1 and try to update just its Name. Expected result Creating a record refuses when required fields are missing, in the same way updating one does, and names the fields that are missing. Values sent in an unrecognised shape are rejected rather than dropped. Actual result Step 1: an empty body returns 201 Created. The record exists and holds nothing but its automatically-set owner. Five required fields are missing and nothing is said about it. Step 3: returns 201 Created, storing the Name and silently omitting the four other required fields. Step 4: returns 201 Created, and stores none of the five values. The record is blank apart f

NDC-2536.name: CRM: Zoho CRM settings Wonder Travel uses that our CRM can't hold
NDC-2536.desc: Summary We copied Wonder Travel's live Zoho CRM setup onto the staging CRM (NDC-Staging tenant). Almost everything fits. These three things Zoho has and our CRM can't hold. Already done Roles, profiles, modules, fields, layouts, pipeline, email templates, 23 workflow rules, company settings, module names, and the Ordered Items / Purchase Items line-item subforms are all copied and working. Missing More than one currency. Zoho has EGP as home currency plus USD, AED, JOD, KWD, OMR and SAR with exchange rates, and each record can be in its own currency. Our CRM has one company currency and no exchange-rate list. Validation rules on picklist fields. Zoho has two active rules on picklists: Deals "Stage" must be one of C/E/R/S/V, and Calls "Outgoing Call Status" rule. Our CRM refuses to create a validation rule on a picklist field. Related: NDC-2535. Formula that adds up subform rows. Zoho's Sales Orders and Purchase Orders have Sub Total (sum of the line-item Totals) and Grand Total (Sub Total - Discount + Tax + Adjustment). Our formula field has no SUM over a subform (functions offered: abs, coalesce, concat, if, …), so Sub Total and Grand Total can't be built. A subform sub-field also can't be a formula, so line Amount and Total don't calculate either. Already filed (not repeated here) Scoring rules: NDC-2030. Environment staging-crm.taviportal.com, NDC-Staging tenant, 25 October 2026, owner account. Zoho side read-only from the live Wonder Travel org.

NDC-2386.name: Pipelines | Settings › Pipelines stays on "Loading board…" when opened directly or reloaded

NDC-1598.name: [Enhancement] Modules and Fields | Field Listing page is missing a layout filter
NDC-1598.desc: Summary The Field Listing page shows which layouts each field belongs to, but offers no way to filter the list by layout. On a module with several layouts, there is no way to answer "which fields are on this layout?" without reading every row. Zoho provides a layout dropdown on the same screen, with an All Layouts option alongside each individual layout. Current Behavior Settings → Modules and Fields → Leads → Fields → Field Listing lists every field on the module in one flat list. The page offers a search box for field names and data types, and a Create and Edit Fields button. There is no layout control. The Layouts column shows each field's layouts as chips, but a field on several layouts is truncated — the Name field shows FieldPermissions, New Layout, New Layout 2 and then "+1", so the fourth cannot be seen. The search box matches field names and data types only, so a layout name cannot be searched for either. Proposed Behavior Add a layout dropdown to the Field Listing toolbar, in line with the search box and the Create and Edit Fields button. The dropdown lists every layout on the module, plus an All Layouts option, with a tick marking the current selection. Selecting a layout filters the list to the fields on that layout. Selecting All Layouts restores the full list, including fields that belong to no layout at all. Reference Zoho CRM places this control on the equivalent screen (Leads → Fields → Field Listing). Its dropdown offers All Layouts followed by each layout by name, and defaults to a single layout rather than All Layouts. Whether to match that default or open on All Layouts is a decision worth making deliberately. Environment App: TAVI CRM — https://crm.taviportal.com/settings/modules-and-fields/841043e1-c078-41f9-8d6e-dfd61bee45c3 Leads module, Fields

NDC-1603.name: Recycle Bin | Restoring a record with duplicate data to a unique field is accepted without validation.
NDC-1603.desc: Summary A record restored from the Recycle Bin is reinstated even when its value in a unique field is already used by a live record. The restore reports success and the module ends up with two records holding the same value. Editing a record to that same value is correctly rejected, so the rule is enforced on normal edits but not on restore. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings → Modules and Fields → Leads, open a layout, and set the Name field to unique. Save. Return to the Leads module and note a record that already exists — here, one named RCB-020. Go to Settings → Data Administration → Recycle Bin. Tick a deleted record that has the same name, RCB-020, and click Restore. Confirm. Return to the Leads module and look at the list. For comparison, edit a third record and set its Name to RCB-020, then save. Expected Result The restore is refused because the value is already in use, and the item is reported as failed with a conflict message. The operator is told which item could not be restored and why, with the option to rename it on restore or skip it. A unique field never holds the same value on two live records, whichever route the data arrives by. Actual Result The restore reports success and the record is reinstated. The module now lists two records named RCB-020 — the record count goes from 9 to 10 and both rows appear. Editing a third record to the same name is rejected with "Name is already in use by another record." No warning appears at any point during the restore. Environment App: TAVI CRM — https://crm.taviportal.com, Leads module, layout New Layout Name field set to unique POST /api/v1/audit/recycle-bin/restore returned 200 with the item listed under succeeded Browser: Google Chrome 152.0.7977.83 OS: Windows 10 (x86) Viewport: 1272 × 866 Captured: 13 Sep 2026,

NDC-1232.name: [Enhancement] Data Types | The header row scrolls out of view and columns are too narrow, wrapping values across multiple lines
NDC-1232.desc: Summary Two problems make the Data Types table hard to use. The header row is not frozen. Scrolling down the list moves the header off screen, leaving a grid of checkbox columns with no labels. Since most columns are capability checkboxes that look identical, there is no way to tell which capability a given column controls once the header has scrolled away. Note the header row: Label, Category, Source, Create Layout Rule, Create Validation Rule, Edit Properties, Mark Required, Permanently Delete, and a further column cut off at the right edge. Look at the Label, Category and Source columns and note how their values wrap. Scroll down the list past the first few rows. Look for the header row. Try to identify which capability each checkbox column controls. Note the horizontal scrollbar and the column truncated to "Re…". Expected Result The header row should stay fixed while the list scrolls, so column meanings remain visible at all times. Column widths should suit their content: datatype names and category and source values should fit on a single line. Capability columns should be sized to their headings so each is identifiable. The table should fit the available width, or make clear that further columns exist to the right. Row heights should be consistent and compact. Actual Result The he

NDC-2130.name: Custom Views | Arabic UI: 'records' in the record count and the sort label's field/direction are not translated
NDC-2130.desc: Summary Arabic UI: 'records' in the record count and the sort label's field/direction are not translated. Found by test case CVS-L01 - The picker, editor, manage pages, Kanban and Split are fully translated in Arabic, including user-count plurals. NDC-1693.name: Modules and Fields | Creating a new module returns 500 Internal Server Error.
NDC-1693.desc: Summary A new module cannot be created. Submitting the Create module dialog with a valid display name and module key fails with an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error from the server, and the module is not created. The error is returned for more than one teamspace, so it is not specific to a particular one. No client-side validation message is shown — the request is accepted and then fails on the server. Steps to Reproduce Go to Settings > Customization > Modules and Fields. Click "+ Create New Module". Choose a teamspace from the Teamspace dropdown. Enter a display name, for example "testModule". Leave the module key as generated, for example "testmodule", and leave Description empty. Click Create. Repeat with a different teamspace selected. Expected Result The module should be created and appear in the Modules list. If the request cannot be completed, the message should explain what is wrong and what to do about it. A valid request should not produce a server error. Actual Result The request fails with HTTP 500 Internal Server Error. The message shown is "An unexpected error occurred. Trace id: …", displayed both inline in the dialog and as a toast. The module is not created and does not appear in the Modules list. The same failure occurs for more than one teamspace, so it is not teamspace-specific. No console errors are produced — the failure is entirely server-side. New modules cannot be created at all through this dialog. Environment App: Anyware CRM — https://crm.taviportal.com/settings/modules-and-fields Teamspaces tried: "test" and "CRM Teamspace" Module attempted: display name "testModule", key "testmodule" Browser: Edge 152.0.7977.83 OS: Windows 10 (x86) Viewport: 1272 x 473 Reporter: Mahmoud Mohamed Captured: 16 Sept 2026, 10:48 UTC Attachment Attachment
